name: March 26, 2024 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 26, 2024
  CITY HALL, MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  9:00 A.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Lawrence called the meeting to order at 9:05 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Fireball Lawrence; Vice Chair Julia Holland; and Commissioners Lotte
  Cherin (arrived at 9:09 a.m.), Barry Haldeman, and Peter Jones

  ABSENT: Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Alexis Brown, Deputy
  City Manager; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Jones moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Cherin absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the meeting agenda was properly posted on
  March 20, 2024.

ITEM 1.  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  1.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops had
  concluded at all Malibu schools, and staff were compiling poems and
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  artwork for the 2024 Student and Art anthology. She stated artwork from
  Webster Elementary School would be displayed at the Poetry Summit.

  Commissioner Cherin arrived at 9:09 a.m.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Vice Chair Holland stated the Leigh McCloskey Art Exhibition Opening
  Reception on March 24 went well. She stated Mr. McCloskey was honored
  and thankful for the opportunity to show his artwork.

  Chair Lawrence indicated agreement with Vice Chair Holland and thanked
  her for a great Question and Answer session during the opening reception.

  Commissioner Haldeman stated he was impressed with the number of
  people who attended the event.

  Commissioner Jones thanked Chair Lawrence and Vice Chair Holland for
  their commitment to enhancing the Malibu City Gallery.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  None.

  4.  Social Media

  Chair Lawrence stated social media posts should be done once a day.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the City's media team could work with 99.1 KBUU radio to promote art
  programs.

  Vice Chair Holland suggested adding information in the Malibu Times
  calendar section.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Cherin moved, and Vice Chair Holland seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the February 27, 2024 Malibu
  Arts Commission Regular Meeting.
  2. Malibu Arts Commission Rules of Procedure and Decorum
  Recommended Action: Adopt Malibu Arts Commission Resolution No. 24-01
  Rules of Procedure and Decorum amending Section 4.C. Regular Meeting
  Schedule.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Guidelines for Temporary Public Art
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the draft Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance
  of Temporary Art Criteria and Guidelines; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated artists would provide a letter to prove they had community support for their
  project.

  In response to Commissioner Cherin, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that the Commission would review proposals for temporary art.

  The Commission indicated agreement to remove: "There should be a compelling
  reason to install temporary artwork on City property, such as the artwork's
  relevance within the site's natural, cultural, historical, social, or environmental
  context," and "The artist should have community support."

  In response to Community Services Riesgo, Commissioner Haldeman requested
  that the requirement of three letters of community support be changed to one letter.

  The Commission indicated agreement to revise the artist-required proposal item
  "Three letters of community support, which may include up to one letter for a
  Malibu Arts Commissioner" to state "One letter of community support, which may
  include a letter from a Malibu Arts Commissioner."

  Commissioner Jones stated a risk assessment should be completed to ensure the
  safety and stability of a sculpture.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the artist loan agreement would
  include language regarding discoloration, liability, and a risk assessment.

  The Commission indicated agreement to remove: "Thorough ADA compliance
  review."
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 26, 2024
  Page 4 of 6

  Commissioner Haldeman stated artists from any location could submit a proposal
  for temporary artwork.

  Chair Lawrence indicated agreement with Commissioner Haldeman. He stated that
  mailed artwork should not be the City's responsibility due to the high probability
  of it being damaged.

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the artist would be responsible for all costs
  associated with the temporary artwork.

  The Commission agreed to remove: "Malibu residents will be given priority."

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Commissioner Jones seconded a motion to approve
  the Malibu Arts Commission Acceptance of Temporary Art Criteria and Guidelines
  with the following revisions: 1) Removing: "There should be a compelling reason
  to install temporary artwork on City property, such as the artwork's relevance
  within the site's natural, cultural, historical, social, or environmental context" from
  the Criteria for Approval section; 2) Removing: "The artist should have community
  support" from the Criteria for Approval section; 3) Revising: "Three letters of
  community support, which may include up to one letter from a Malibu Arts
  Commissioner" to state "One letter of community support, which may be from a
  Malibu Arts Commissioner" as a required artist proposal item; 4) Revising: "If
  required, structural engineer drawings to ensure the safety and stability of the
  proposed installation" to state "If required, structural engineer drawings to ensure
  the safety and stability of the proposed installation to conduct a risk assessment" as
  an Artist Required Proposal Items; 5) Removing: "Thorough ADA compliance
  review" from the Artist Required Proposal Items section; and 6) Removing:
  "Malibu residents will be given priority" under the General Guidelines for
  Temporary Art Displays section. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated that the Public Works Commission had tabled the Neighborhood
  Beautification Program since they were focused on Pacific Coast Highway Safety.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  City-Owned Vacant Land Outreach Plan
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive a presentation on City-owned vacant lots; and
  2) Provide input to City staff and consultant on an outreach plan.

  Community Services Director Riesgo introduced Deputy City Manager Brown.

  Deputy City Manager Brown presented the staff report and introduced Alyson
  Nichols from Tripepi Smith & Associates.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of March 26, 2024
  Page 5 of 6

Commissioner Jones stated staff should review written agreements to determine
land use and limitations.

Deputy City Manager Brown stated that the deed· restnct1ons and property
limitations had been reviewed by staff. She stated a comprehensive list of
community input was required.

In response to Commissioner Jones, Deputy City Manager Brown stated hiring a
landscape architect would assume the City knew what would be built on each
property, which was in the conceptual stage.

Commissioner Cherin indicated agreement with Commissioner Jones.

Deputy City Manager Brown stated that the Planning Department would complete
property assessments and clarified that Commissioner Jones requested the
involvement of a landscape architect as part of the outreach process.

Commissioner Jones stated a landscape architect could confirm environmental
limitations.

Commissioner Haldeman stated mailers were a successful outreach tactic.

In response to Ms. Nichols, Chair Lawrence stated outreach should be done with
Malibu Facebook groups.

Vice Chair Holland suggested posting information on the Nextdoor platform.

Commissioner Cherin suggested coordinating multiple focus groups.

Commissioner Jones suggested using MailChimp with project images.

In response to Ms. Nichols, the Commission stated multiple hybrid meetings at
various City locations would be ideal. The Commission suggested recording
meetings.

Chair Lawrence stated outreach should be six months but would understand if the
process was one year.

Vice Chair Holland indicated agreement with Chair Lawrence.

Commissioner Haldemann stated a community survey should be open for six
weeks.

Deputy City Manager Brown stated the outreach timeline would include gathering
public input, surveying the community, meeting with stakeholders, and compiling
a report.

  Commissioner Haldeman requested that businesses be included in the outreach
  process.

  In response to Ms. Nichols, the Commission stated keywords would be locals only,
  benefitting Malibu, open space, and for Malibu residents.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Chumash Day
  Powwow and Intertribal Gathering and poetry programs. She stated the April 23 ,
  2024 Regular Meeting would start at 9:30 a.m.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Chair Lawrence stated Sue Wong attended the Leigh McCloskey opening art
  reception and the Ad Hoc was working to potentially have her exhibit at the Malibu
  City Gallery.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Malibu Lumber Yard

ADJOURNMENT

  At 11 :04 a.m. , Chair Lawrence adjourned the meeting.
